correctness.rationale: A deleted six-set yields a disconnected C_n² survivor iff its cyclic word contains at least two deleted one-runs of length ≥2. One-deleted-vertex gaps are bypassed by cycle-square edges while gaps of ≥2 split surviving components. For r=2,3,4 runs, compositions of six with ≥2 long runs number 3,7,6. Distribute k zero gaps by C(k−1,r−1), count n/r rotations to derive f5. Five-vertex nonfaces are exactly an interval run of five or an independent 5-set in the ordinary cycle, yielding f4 by subtracting n+n/(k+1) C(k+1,5) from C(n,5). Every four-subset extends to a qualifying six-facet by adding ≤2 vertices, so the lower face vector is binomial. The alternating Euler sum reduces to the stated quartic. Independent graph connectivity and downward-closure tests for k=3…7 agree; supplied verification source checks k≤14, neither is an infinite proof. Conditional shellability implication only.
residual_risks: Extension argument at small k requires care; exact finite enumeration corroborates base ranges while run proof is infinite.
No unconditional wedge theorem when shellability is not established.

final_claim: For all integers k≥3, n=k+6, Δ_k(C_n²) has f_j=C(n,j+1) for j=0,…,3, f_4=k(k+6)(k²+3k+8)/6 and f_5=(k−1)(k+6)(3k²−k+8)/12, giving reduced χ=−(k⁴+2k³−21k²+18k+8)/8. Any wedge of 5-spheres description is conditional on an unproved general shellability conjecture.
limitations: Computer replay finite k only, not used as all-k proof.
